verdict.rationale: x402 replaces card numbers with per-payment signed authorizations. The 'upto' scheme authorizes a capped maximum. Batch settlement uses explicit escrow with cryptographically signed limits and refund/withdrawal semantics. Agents pay from a dedicated agentic wallet funded with USDC. This amounts to bounded, seller-bound payment authority, but nothing documents a user-issued credential where the user sets an agent's spend caps, expiry or merchant allowlist. Missing for 10: a user-configurable scoped credential or spend policy for the agent, documented expiry controls, merchant-restriction controls, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can hand my agent a scoped, limited-use payment credential — amount limits, expiry, merchant restrictions — instead of a raw card number

citations.quote: Escrow is explicit, limits are cryptographically signed, and buyers retain defined refund and withdrawal semantics.
